summary: Norio Koyama works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami, and held an attested professorship at Taisho University in 2014.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Noritoshi Aramaki completed studies and a doctoral degree at Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (~1974–1981, 2000), Osaka University (~1981–1989), Otani University (~2000–2006), and Kyoto Koka Women's University (~2006–2011).

Noriyuki Kudo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who did postgraduate work at Bukkyo University. He lectured at Bukkyo University (attested 1999–2000) and has served as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2026).

Norman Fischer works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Colgate University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, as well as under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, and founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.

Norman Mosley Penzer was a scholar active in Indology and other fields. In 1925, he was attested as a fellow of the Royal Anthropological Institute, Royal Geographical Society, and Geological Society, and a member of the Folklore and Royal Asiatic societies.

Norvin J. Hein worked in Indology and religious studies, studying under Franklin Edgerton. He held a post as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University (attested 1965).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Nosei Fuji studied as an international student at Dongguk University in 1986. His posts include Daegu University (1988), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007), and a professorship at Ryukoku University (attested 2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as Associate Director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo from ~1989 to 2011.

Noémie Verdon works in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2015 under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2019).

Noël Peri specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He taught Western music at Tokyo University of the Arts (1896–1906), founded Mélanges japonais in 1904, and held positions at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1907 and 1911.

Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon and under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Mahasi Sayadaw. He founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as editor and leader (1958–1984) and president (~1958–1988).
Nyingcha Duoji specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Boston University and Harvard University (PhD attested 2014) under Leonard van der Kuijp and Mark Elliott.

Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche studied at Katok and Nyoshul monasteries, and under Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Nyoten Jinbo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami and held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ogyen Trinley Dorje studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (~2001), the 14th Dalai Lama (~2000), Pema Donyo Nyinje, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and Bokar Rinpoche.
Ohryu Matsushima works in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and later held a post there.

Olaf Hansen was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena, Humboldt University of Berlin (~1944–1949), and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969).

Olav Hackstein specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and University of Freiburg (Dr. phil. 1983–1993), later becoming a full professor at the University of Munich in 2008.

Ole Holten Pind worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2004–2009) under Ernst Steinkellner and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.
